prerequisites: Having studied Physics in the last year of high school (Bachillerato)
Prior mathematical knowledge of vector calculus, trigonometry, and derivation and integration of single-variable functions.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical-mathematical description of particle motion and know the magnitudes that quantify it.
Understand the laws and theorems that relate the motion of particles to the causes that provoke it.
Understand the concepts and principles necessary for the study of heat exchange processes in closed systems of ideal gases.
Correctly handle the recommended physical symbology, both in terms of magnitudes and units.
Learn and apply problem-solving strategies related to the different contents of the course.
Acquire skills related to laboratory work and the treatment of measurements and errors.

syllabus_topics: Physical magnitudes. Treatment of measurement errors.
Dynamics of the particle: Work and energy.
Thermometry and calorimetry. First law of thermodynamics.
teaching_methods: Classroom practices/Seminars/Workshops (problem solving, group activities, presentation and defense of problems)
Laboratory practices (equipment handling, simulation/data treatment software, analysis of results and report writing)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if the score in the global exam (CGO) is 3.5 points or higher (out of 10), the final grade (NFO) is calculated as NFO = EvC + (1 – EvC/10) × CGO, where EvC = CPA + CCS + CPL is the continuous assessment grade. A minimum global score of 2.0 points (out of 5.5) is required in continuous assessment; otherwise, the continuous assessment grade becomes zero. If continuous assessment is lost or chosen not to be followed, the final grade (NFE) will be the global exam grade (CGE). Any final score below 5.0 results in a FAIL. For extraordinary calls, the continuous assessment grade (EvC) from the ordinary period can be combined with the extraordinary global exam (CGE) if CGE is 3.5 or higher; otherwise, the final grade is CGE.
